derived.reason: AWS resources are drawn inside the AWS Cloud frame.
AWS resources that belong to a Region are drawn inside that Region's frame.
No Region was given, so ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo) is used.
An Amazon Aurora DB cluster can be created only in a VPC, so a VPC is drawn.
The DB subnet group chosen for an Aurora DB cluster must cover at least two Availability Zones. archwire draws at least two Availability Zones.
No number of Availability Zones was given, so two are used.
archwire gives each Availability Zone one private subnet; no part here is placed in a public subnet.
Regional services that are not placed in a VPC subnet are drawn inside the Region frame and outside the VPC frame.

A Lambda function can be given access to resources in an Amazon VPC by attaching it to the VPC through the private subnets that contain the resources. archwire draws a function that connects to a part in a VPC in that VPC's private subnets.

Every Lambda function runs inside a VPC that Lambda owns and manages; attaching a function to a VPC gives it a network interface that Lambda creates for the chosen subnet and security group combination. archwire draws the attached function once in the private subnet of each Availability Zone.
No subnet was given, so Aurora is placed in private subnets so it is not reachable from the internet.
The Writer goes in the first Availability Zone and Readers in the remaining ones.
